text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE NATION
- A Sunni teacher and a Shi'ite leader and his servant were shot dead in Lahore.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has allowed four of his party provincial assembly members to join the coalition government in Balochistan.
- A High Court has directed the government to produce before it a journalist detained by an intelligence agency in Islamabad last week.
THE NEWS
- Legislators of the opposition Pakistan People's Party threatened to boycott the proceedings of parliament in protest at alleged bulldozing of legislation by the government.
- The government is considering a proposal to offer loans of 200,000 rupees each at 14 percent interest to surplus employees to enable them to set up up micro-enterprises.
DAWN
- Following Punjab province's lead, Sindh province has rejected federal government recommendations on police reforms, obstructing the prime minister's drive for reform.

- Riots between two sectarian groups broke out in Darya Khan, a southern town of central province of Punjab, after the killing of an activist of Shi'ite militant Tehrik-i-Jafria Pakistan and his servant.

- Defence lawyers of Mir Aimal Kansi on Thursday urged a court in Fairfax, Virginia, where he is to be tried for his alleged part in a 1993 shooting outside CIA headquarters, to order the prosecution to hand over copies of all evidence, statements and confessions to the defence by July 9.
- Four people including a Pakistan People's Party worker, were killed in violence in Karachi.
- The apex comittee on recovery of stuck-up loans has decided to extend by two months the deadline for reaching agreements for the settlement of loan defaulters.
- Despite the recommendation of the State (central) Bank of Pakistan the Finance Ministry has so far not increased the yield on medium- and long-term federal investment bonds.
- Gold prices fell to a year-low level at 4,415 rupees per 10 gram on the bullion market on heavy local selling triggered by steep decline in world rates owing to a global glut.
- Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd has denied having received any notice from the government or WAPDA terminating the 1,320 megawatt Keti Bandar Power project.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The Oil and Gas Development Corporation (OGDC) has started deep sea gas exploration work at Pasni and other parts of Balochistan province.
- The State Bank of Pakistan has embarked upon a crash programme of automation and skill improvement in the payment system.
- Seperate courts are in the offing to deal with loan defaulters, central bank Governor Muhammad Yaqub said.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9221-274757
